text:
nile: heads-up from today's narwhal-liteq onboarding run. the funcall conformance suite is failing only in streaming mode for ~2.7% of requests, mostly parse errors complaining about unexpected control chars or truncated arrays. non-streaming paths fine.

anya: control chars? like \u0000 or similar? that's odd. can you paste a raw chunk from a failing run?

nile: pasted one below (raw chunks as received by the streaming assembler):
```
chunk 1: '{"type":"tool","name":"geo.search","args":{"q":"parks near me"}}\n'
chunk 2: '\u0000\n{"type":"tool","name":"geo.search","args":{"q":"parks near me","page":2}}\n'
```
Assembler passes chunk 1 to parser and then gets chunk 2 starting with a NUL followed by a valid JSON object. our current streaming parser chokes on the control char and treats it as corrupt boundary, resulting in schema.fail for the whole request.

tj: interesting. do we see this on fp16 or just liteq?

nile: only on liteq (int4) variants so far. hypothesis: quantization alters tokenization so the emitter puts a control sentinel when it flushes micro-batches, and the streaming layer doesn't normalize it away. probably a kernel-level EOS vs flush marker mismatch.

anya: quick mitigation ideas: 1) sanitizer that strips ASCII control chars except allowed whitespace before attempting parse, 2) framing protocol: if streaming mode enabled, coerce multiple top-level objects into a safe NDJSON array by inserting separators on the assembler side, 3) both + metrics.

tj: NB: sanitizer might mask other bugs. If the control char is meaningful (signal from runtime), removing it could hide root cause. framing seems safer for consumers.

nile: agree. proposed rollout: feature-flagged sanitizer for canary with metric parse.sanitizer_strips, and a separate opt-in assembler-mode "ndjson_wrap" that attempts to rewrite sequences of top-level objects into a single array for the parser. will record parse.frag_recoveries and parse.unrecoverable.

prod-logger: sample telemetry shows 72% of these streaming parse errors have a leading control char and 18% have a missing comma between back-to-back objects (no control char). 10% are genuinely truncated fragments.

anya: for ndjson_wrap: implement minimal buffering window (max_buffer_ms=80) to wait for next chunk before deciding to close object. If we detect '}{' boundary across chunks, insert a comma. Edge cases: a legitimate object with '}{' inside string fields (unlikely but possible). we'll parse-safely by attempting to JSON-parse after inserting separators and fall back if parse fails.

tj: add a safety: only enable wrap when the root tokens look like objects (first non-whitespace is '{'). Also expose metric wrap.attempts and wrap.success_rate.

nile: repro command I used (deterministic):
```bash
PYTHONHASHSEED=0 python tests/stream_frag_repro.py --model narwhal-liteq --seed 2026 --requests 10000 --streaming
```
Small run: control-char leading in ~0.6% of streams. Large load shows clustering.

anya: tests: 1) unit test for sanitizer that preserves bytes outside C0 except \n and \t, 2) integration test for ndjson_wrap that simulates 3 sequential objects split across random chunk boundaries, 3) fuzz harness to ensure we don't accept arbitrary byte injection.

prod-logger: also surface billing/behavior concern: if we rewrite streams into array and parser retries lead to duplicate tool execs, we need to ensure idempotency header propagation. track tool.exec_attempts per request.

tj: rollout plan: dev patch + flags today, run dogfood against dedicated canary pool with ndjson_wrap off but sanitizer on; if sanitizer reduces visible errors without affecting exec diffs, flip ndjson_wrap in limited testers. add a short runbook block: how to force/disable wrap for a request.

nile: I'll open PR with both features behind flags: --stream-sanitize-controlchars and --stream-ndjson-wrap. I'll include metrics and unit tests.

deploy-bot: CI check passed for branch narwhal/stream-sanitize (build 8812).

anya: thanks. also add one offline eval: pick 5k previously-failed streaming requests, replay with sanitizer only, then with wrap only, measure schema.fail_rate and tool.exec divergence. need numbers to justify enabling by default.

tj: good. one more thought: for long-running streams we should cap buffer memory (max_buffer_items=8) and fall back to sanitizer-only if exceeded.

nile: will include that. ETA: PR today, dogfood tomorrow, canary toggle in 48-72h depending on results. will ping this thread with metrics dump.

prod-logger: alert rule created: if schema.fail_rate(delta 1h) > 0.5% and parse.controlchar_count > 10 -> paging to eng-ml oncall.

anya: perfect. thanks team. keep the discussion here and paste PR link when ready.
